Macro engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Macro rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app close-up capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Macro & Macro Control — Apple Camera feature that automatically switches to the ultra-wide lens for extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance on supported iPhone models. Labeled 微距 or 微距近拍 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • Ultra-wide lens auto-switch & minimum focus distance — system and app logic that engages 0.5x macro framing when the subject is close. Your listing may mention Auto Macro or Macro Control; building lens-switch pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Close-up capture UI & focus lock — separate in-app surfaces where buyers frame flower, insect, texture, or product detail shots. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; macro sample photo production is outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVFoundation & capture sessions — camera session code that reads frames and drives the viewfinder at close range. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Macro value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Macro support in the binary.

A working Macro or Macro Control story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Macro vs Action Mode vs Cinematic Mode vs Photographic Styles vs Portrait vs Night Mode vs Action Button vs Camera Control — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge eight Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Macro and Macro Control — extreme close-up still photography — not video stabilization, not cinematic depth-of-field, not tone presets, not background blur, not low-light modes, and not hardware buttons:

  • Macro & Macro Control close-up photography (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Macro", "Macro Control", "Auto Macro", "Close-up", "Extreme close-up", "0.5x ultra-wide macro", 微距, 微距近拍, 微距控制. Still-photo extreme close-ups at minimum focus distance — flower, insect, texture, product detail shots.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖, 手持稳定视频. Video stabilization — not still-photo macro close-ups. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not macro still photography.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, Rich Contrast, Vibrant, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度, 鲜明, 暖色, 冷色. Photo color grading — not macro close-up framing. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.
  • Portrait mode listing copy (different) — background blur and depth-of-field when photographing people or objects: Portrait mode, 人像模式, 景深虚化, 背景虚化. Subject-background separation — not macro minimum-focus-distance close-ups.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light photography — not daytime flower or insect macro detail shots.
  • Action Button listing copy (different) — the physical side button on iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 family devices configured under Settings → Action Button: 操作按钮, 灵动按钮. Hardware button assignment — not Macro toggle marketing. Covered on our Action Button guide.
  • Camera Control listing copy (different) — iPhone 16 physical camera button with light press, half-press, slide, and click gestures: Camera Control, 相机控制. Hardware capture control — not Macro Control close-up photography framing. See Camera Control guide.

Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Macro captures extreme close-up stills. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Portrait mode blurs backgrounds. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Action Button assigns a hardware side button. Camera Control is a dedicated capture control. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Macro-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Close-up photography listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Macro features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Macro phrasing

US pages use "Macro", "Macro Control", "Auto Macro", "Close-up", "Extreme close-up", "0.5x ultra-wide macro", or "Minimum focus distance." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 微距 for the general macro feature, 微距近拍 for close-up still capture, and 微距控制 when your English listing brands Macro Control as a toggle or slider. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing macro capabilities your app does not support.

0.5x ultra-wide vs standard lens framing

Macro marketing often shows the automatic switch to 0.5x ultra-wide for close subjects. Chinese buyers expect concise labels on gallery frames: 0.5倍微距, 超广角微距, or 自动微距 when Auto Macro is the hero — not English "0.5x" pasted through machine translation without context.

Subject types per frame

Screenshot overlays differ by subject — flower petals, insect eyes, fabric texture, product labels, coin details. Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 花卉微距 for flower close-ups, 昆虫细节 for insect detail, 纹理近拍 for texture macros — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Macro vs generic close-up zoom

When your English listing markets both Apple's Macro branding and generic "close-up photography" or "detail shots" terms, zh-Hans overlays may use 微距 for Apple's branded toggle and 近拍 or 细节拍摄 for generic close-up search intent — distinct buyer promises with different screenshot vocabulary on the same product page.

Do not conflate with Action Mode, Cinematic Mode, or Photographic Styles

Macro captures extreme close-up stills at minimum focus distance. Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video — different buyer promise. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Photographic Styles adjusts still-photo tone at capture. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need macro search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 微距, 微距近拍, and 微距控制 each signal different intent from Action Mode 动作模式 keywords or Photographic Styles 摄影风格 keywords.

No. Ultra-wide macro switching, minimum-focus-distance capture, and in-app close-up flows control device behavior — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback.

How is this different from Action Mode, Cinematic Mode, Photographic Styles, Portrait mode, Night Mode, Action Button, or Camera Control?

Macro copy markets extreme close-up still photography — 微距, 微距近拍, 微距控制. Action Mode copy markets handheld video stabilization — 动作模式, 运动防抖. Cinematic Mode copy markets shallow-depth cinematic video — 浅景深电影效果视频. Photographic Styles copy markets still-photo tone presets — 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Portrait mode copy markets background blur — 人像模式. Night Mode copy markets low-light capture — 夜间模式. Action Button copy markets the physical side button — 操作按钮. Camera Control copy markets dedicated capture hardware — 相机控制. Each surface has separate screenshot vocabulary.

Should zh-Hans copy use 微距, 微距近拍, or 微距控制?

Each appears in Chinese storefront and search contexts. AppLocale picks phrasing that matches your English listing claims and screenshot overlays — 微距 for the general feature, 微距近拍 for close-up still capture, 微距控制 for Macro Control branding — without inventing capabilities your app does not support.
